blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: As multimodal AI systems are becoming our everyday thought partners, the shift towards studying how users transfer control to these systems becomes especially urgent. In this paper, we report an overview of findings from an online study with n=56 AI-literate participants and 392 Video Question Answering trials. After inspecting each multimodal AI response, participants rated task-specific trust and selected one of three intended policies for an analogous future task: reject AI assistance, use it with verification, or delegate fully to the AI. Within participants, post-interaction trust strongly predicted the user's delegation choices (OR=14.97, 95% CI [7.14,31.37]). Trust and delegation nevertheless remained distinct. Verification was the dominant policy and often co-occurred with high trust. Delegation also increased with task order after adjustment for momentary and participant-level trust (OR=1.22, 95% CI [1.02,1.45]), indicating an experience-related component that self-reported trust ratings alone could not capture. These findings motivate a shift from intended delegation to a non-intrusive observation of how delegation is enacted in collaborative human-AI tasks. We therefore conclude by proposing enacted delegation traces as a methodological framework for future studies of multimodal and agentic AI use.
blocks.zh: 随着多模式AI系统正成为我们日常的思想伙伴,转向研究用户如何向这些系统转移控制变得特别紧迫. 在本文中,我们汇报了一项在线研究的总结结果,参与者为n=56 AI识字者和392个视频问答试验。 在检查了每一份多式大赦国际答复之后,与会者对特定任务的信任进行了评分,并为类似的未来任务选择了三项预期政策之一:拒绝大赦国际的援助,加以核查,或向大赦国际充分授权。 在参与者中,互动后信任强烈预测了用户代表团的选择(OR=14.97,95%CI [7.14,31.37]). 然而,信任和代表团仍然不同。 核查是主导政策,而且常常是高度信任的共同行为。 在调整了瞬间信任和参与者级信任(OR=1.22,95% CI [1.02,1.45])后,代表团也随任务顺序而增加,表明仅自报的信任评级无法捕捉到与经验相关的部分. 这些结论促使人们从打算授权转变为对授权是如何在人类-AI合作任务中实施的无侵犯性的观察。 因此,我们最后提议,颁布代表团跟踪法,作为今后研究使用多式和代理AI的方法框架。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: A typical day in the life of a 2026 knowledge worker may look like this. The day begins in an online meeting, where an AI assistant listens quietly in the background, turning the discussion into notes. Later, while drafting a technical report, they ask another assistant to revise a paragraph and keep only the most useful suggestions. A scientific claim looks useful, but not quite safe to trust, so they verify it against external sources. They also need a chart to accompany the text, so they ask another AI assistant to write the code for generating it, before adding their final touches.

Human agency and oversight are central to European frameworks for Trustworthy AI and are explicitly reflected in the AI Act High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (2019) ; European Parliament and Council of the European Union (2024) . Yet translating
these principles into interaction-level evaluation remains an open challenge: technical properties such as transparency, robustness, and accountability Chander et al. (2025) ; Novelli et al. (2024) do not by themselves reveal how users retain or transfer control while working with an AI system. We therefore ask: how can human oversight be made observable in practice while AI carries out part or all of a task?

blocks.en:
We propose delegation as a complementary lens for studying human oversight as it is enacted in interaction with multimodal AI systems. Delegation concerns which parts of a
task users hand over to an AI system, how they inspect or verify its outputs,
and when they intervene to change or reclaim control. In this view, a system may satisfy
technical and regulatory requirements for trustworthiness while still eliciting poorly calibrated
delegation. For instance, a user may trust an AI system while still deciding to verify its output or completely avoid full delegation for tasks they perceive as personally meaningful or risky. The same user, nonetheless, may delegate to a less trusted system when time,
fatigue, or lack of expertise makes independent work costly. For this reason, we distinguish: trustworthiness , as the properties of the system and its deployment; trust , as the user’s situated perception of those properties Mayer et al. (1995) ; and delegation , as the observable
transfer of control over task execution and decision authority between the human and the AI system Lee and See (2004) . This perspective is also relevant to the Explainable AI (XAI) field: an explanation or inspectable representation can support oversight not only by changing trust, but by shaping how users delegate to the AI the system.

The contribution of this paper is twofold. First, we provide a task-level account of how trust, repeated experience, and the availability of an inspectable graph representation for the model answers relate to
intended delegation among AI-literate users,
whom we selected as a deliberate first population for studying these dynamics
during repeated multimodal interaction (Section 3 and 4). Second, we introduce enacted delegation traces as a general framework
for studying how responsibility is redistributed during collaborative tasks
across user populations and application contexts (Sections 5 and 6). We
formalise these traces through the scope of control transfer, the oversight actions performed after delegation, and the recovery of control. We then
outline how these elements may be observed under varying time pressure,
perceived AI competence, and task stakes. Experimental results reported in this paper measure intended delegation only; the enacted-delegation framework introduced in Sections 5–6 is a methodological proposal motivated by these findings that has not yet been implemented or validated.
Our proposed framing positions delegation as
a measurable object for evaluating the quality of oversight supported by
multimodal and agentic AI systems.

In the paper, we use a focused empirical result to motivate a methodological
position.
Video Question Answering provides a controlled multimodal setting in which users must judge whether an AI system has correctly represented objects, actions, and temporal relations before deciding how much control to retain. From the standpoint of XAI, it also enables a
comparison between a textual answer and an editable spatio-temporal graph that exposes part of the represented video situation for inspection. Thus, we designed a repeated Video Question Answering study, where participants rated trust after each response and selected whether they would reject AI assistance, use it with retained control, or delegate fully on an analogous task. Higher-than-usual trust strongly predicted stronger intended delegation, while retained control remained common even at
high trust. Exploratory findings further suggest that graph-supported presentation was associated with stronger delegation. Together, these findings show that delegation captures how users allocate oversight across repeated interaction in ways that trust ratings alone leave only partly visible.

blocks.en: 2 Background and Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 背景和有关工作

blocks.en: Trust has long been treated as a central construct for explaining how people use automated systems. In classic accounts, it describes a willingness to accept vulnerability to another actor Mayer et al. (1995) , while appropriate reliance concerns whether users rely on automation when it is capable and withhold reliance when it is not Lee and See (2004) . This distinction is important for human-AI interaction because trust remains a subjective judgement, whereas reliance and delegation become visible in how users allocate control. Delegation is especially relevant for systems that do more than provide advice. Yet empirical work still tends to study the users’ post-interaction reactions to AI recommendations more often than the conditions under which users are prepared to transfer control. Gomez et al., for instance, found delegation in only a small fraction of the human-AI interaction sequences reviewed in their survey Gomez et al. (2025) . Recent studies have begun to operationalise delegation more directly, either through willingness to delegate a repeated perceptual task Mehrotra et al. (2024) , or through behavioural traces of whether teams allow an AI partner to answer on their behalf Gor et al. (2026) . These works motivate measuring delegation as a construct related to trust, but analytically distinct from it.
blocks.zh: 长期以来,信任一直被视为解释人们如何使用自动化系统的中心结构。 在经典的叙述中,它描述了接受另一个演员Mayer等人(1995年)的脆弱性的意愿,而适当的依赖则涉及用户是否在有能力时依赖自动化,在不是Lee和See(2004年)时是否不依赖自动化。 这种区分对人与AI的互动很重要,因为信任仍然是主观判断,而依赖和授权则在用户如何分配控制方面变得明显. 授权对于不只是提供咨询的系统特别相关。 然而,实证工作仍然倾向于比用户准备转移控制的条件更经常地研究用户对AI建议的互动后反应. 例如,Gomez等人在其调查Gomez等人(2025年)所审查的人类-AI相互作用序列中,只有一小部分发现有代表团。 最近的研究已经开始使代表团更直接地运作,要么是愿意将反复的感知任务委托给梅赫罗特拉等人(2024年),要么是通过团队是否允许AI伙伴代表他们回答戈尔等人(2026年)的行为痕迹. 这些工作促使人们将权力下放作为一种与信任有关的结构加以衡量,但从分析角度来说却与信任有所区别。

blocks.en: Delegation also connects to established work on human-automation function allocation. Parasuraman et al. distinguish types and levels of automation across information acquisition, analysis, decision selection, and action implementation Parasuraman and Riley (1997) . Pritchett et al. frame function allocation as assigning work across human and automated agents, highlighting potential mismatches between responsibility and authority Pritchett et al. (2014) . More recent human-AI research Adam et al. (2024) shows that whether delegation is initiated by a system or user can affect system acceptance. From an Explainable AI (XAI) perspective, explanations can support appropriate reliance by helping users distinguish when AI advice should or should not be followed Schemmer et al. (2023) ; Mehrotra et al. (2024) . More generally, making the evidence or intermediate representation behind an answer inspectable can support oversight by giving users a basis for checking and revising AI contributions Cosseddu et al. (2026) .

blocks.en: The distinction between reported trust and delegation is particularly underexplored in multimodal AI, compared to language-based AI models and tasks. Research on vision-language models has largely focused on model-centric trustworthiness metrics, including hallucination, robustness, and benchmark performance, while fewer studies examine how users interpret repeated multimodal outputs and translate these evaluations into delegation decisions Chiatti et al. (2025) . Benchmarks such as VHELM and MultiTrust broaden evaluation beyond accuracy by considering several dimensions of multimodal model behaviour Lee et al. (2024) ; Zhang et al. (2024) . Public agent arenas Lu et al. (2024) ; Chou et al. (2025) move closer to situated use by collecting open-ended interactions and preference judgements. However, user preferences do not show how trust evolves across repeated tasks, nor how users retain and transfer their judgment or control over a task. A co-evolutionary view of human-AI interaction further suggests that these choices should be studied across repeated encounters, as both user strategies and system capabilities change through use Pedreschi et al. (2025) .

Lee等人(2024年);Zhang等人(2024年)。 公共代理商Lu等人(2024年);Chou等人(2025年)通过收集开放式互动和偏好判断,更接近于定位使用。 然而,用户偏好没有显示信任如何在重复的任务中演化,也没有显示用户如何保留和转移对某项任务的判断或控制权. 对人与AI互动的共同进化观点进一步表明,这些选择应该通过反复的接触来研究,因为用户策略和系统能力都通过使用Pedreschi等人(2025年)而改变.

blocks.en: Our enacted-delegation perspective builds on these ongoing efforts by focusing on how control transfer during task execution, answer inspection, and recovery of control unfold behaviourally during interaction. We begin exploring Video Question Answering tasks, where users must assess whether a system has correctly interpreted objects, actions, and temporal relations in a video. The STAR benchmark is well suited to this setting because its questions depend on situated reasoning over structured events Wu et al. (2021) . In such tasks, a fluent textual answer can conceal the intermediate representation on which the answer depends. Graph-based presentations offer one way to expose this intermediate layer by making entities and relations inspectable Mitra et al. (2024) ; Lusha et al. (2025) . In our study, we treat graphs as an interface-level presentation model rather than as a guarantee of correctness. It externalises part of the represented video situation, gives users a concrete object to inspect and edit, and allows us to test the effects of a more interactive interface on self-reported trust and delegation choices.

STAR基准非常适合这一设定,因为它的问题取决于在结构化事件(2021年)中的位置推理。 在这种任务中,流利的文字答案可以掩盖答案所依赖的中间代表. 基于图表的演示为暴露这一中间层提供了一种方法,使实体和关系可以检查Mitra等人(2024年);Lusha等人(2025年)。 在我们的研究中,我们把图表当作一个界面级的演示模型,而不是作为正确性的保证. 它将部分代表的视频状况外部化,给用户一个检查和编辑的具体对象,并使我们能够测试一个更互动的界面对自我报告的信任和代表团选择的影响.

blocks.en: We recruited participants through internal student mailing lists, student-representative channels, the AIRLab LinkedIn account, and campus leaflets with QR codes. Of 101 respondents who completed the pre-screening and consent questionnaire, 87 accessed the study platform and 56 completed a full study session (i.e., exactly 7 trials). Participation was voluntary and uncompensated, and participants were informed that the study would require approximately 15 minutes. One participant completed three sessions; to avoid disproportionate weighting, we retained only their first completed session for inference. The final sample therefore comprised N = 56 N=56 participants and 392 analysed task observations.

blocks.en:
Each retained participant completed one guided practice task followed by exactly seven analytic Video Question Answering trials derived from the STAR benchmark Wu et al. (2021) . The analytic task set comprised the same seven selected STAR sequence items across participants; these required connecting actions occurring at different points in an everyday video and determining their temporal order. System responses were generated in advance with Gemini 2.5 Flash so that participants assigned to the same experimental condition encountered stable and comparable stimuli. We restricted the STAR material to temporal sequence questions because preliminary experiments Lusha et al. (2025) found temporal and predictive questions among the most challenging for the Gemini 2.5 Flash. Since predictive questions in STAR include relevant answer evidence only in the ground-truth graphs, but not in the accompanying video clips, we limited our analysis to sampled temporal questions to enable a fair comparison between text-only and graph-supported variants. In each trial, participants
first watched the video and answered the multiple-choice question. They then
inspected a response presented as coming from a generic multimodal AI, without knowing any details about the specific model used for generating answers. We tested four different website variants enabling controlled experimental conditions, summarised in Figure 1 . Depending on
the group assignment, users were exposed on either text-only answers or text accompanied by an editable
spatio-temporal graph. Moreover, two samples served as control group: i.e., users thought they were evaluating AI-generated answers when in fact they were presented with ground truth data. To control for the presence of errors in the AI-generated responses, a later participant cohort encountered deliberately
erroneous responses. The present paper does not delve into the analysis of condition effects.
Here we simply provide an overview of the pooled effects among trust, intended delegation, and task
order, with condition indicators retained as covariates. No a priori or post-hoc power analyses were conducted: small and uneven between-condition samples are treated as exploratory rather than precisely estimated intervention effects.

blocks.en: 5 Position: From Intended to Enacted Delegation
blocks.zh: 5 立场:从原定代表团改为正式代表团

blocks.en: The intended delegation item used in the study we just overviewed was task-specific, temporally close to the trust rating, and preserved verification (i.e., delegation with retained control) as an explicit oversight policy. These properties made it useful for showing that trust and delegation can be measured together during repeated multimodal AI interaction. At the same time, the measure remained separated from the collaborative process itself. Participants did not hand over part of the current task, their choice did not alter the workflow, and no performance or effort consequences followed from the selected policy. The verification option also compressed behaviours that may differ substantially in practice, such as briefly checking a salient video segment, reconstructing the answer independently, or correcting an intermediate representation before accepting the AI contribution, for instance.
blocks.zh: 我们刚才概述的研究中使用的预定代表团项目是针对具体任务、在时间上接近信任等级的,并保留了核查(即保留控制权的代表团)作为明确的监督政策。 这些特性有助于表明在重复的多式联运AI互动中可以一起衡量信任和授权。 同时,这一措施仍然与协作进程本身分开。 与会者没有交出目前任务的一部分,他们的选择没有改变工作流程,选定的政策也没有带来业绩或努力的后果。 核查办法还压缩了实践中可能存在很大差异的行为,例如简短地检查一个显著的视频段,独立地重建答案,或者在接受AI贡献之前纠正中间代表.

blocks.en: We therefore propose moving from intended delegation to enacted delegation traces . We define enacted delegation traces as the observable redistribution of task responsibility between a human and an AI system during an ongoing activity. In this view, delegation is the behavioural process through which users decide what the AI should do, what they will inspect, and when they will reclaim control. The relevant unit of analysis is no longer only the final decision to accept or reject assistance, but the trace of delegations and interventions that occurs while the task is being completed.
blocks.zh: 因此,我们建议从预定的代表团转向制定代表团的痕迹。 我们把已颁布授权的痕迹定义为在一项正在进行的活动中,在人类和人工智能系统之间可观察到的任务责任的重新分配。 这种观点认为,授权是用户决定AI应该做什么,检查什么,何时恢复控制权的行为过程. 相关的分析单位不再仅仅是接受或拒绝援助的最后决定,而是在任务完成时代表团和发言的踪迹。

blocks.en:
For a task episode t t , we represent enacted delegation as a compact trace: 𝒟 t = ⟨ s t , o t , r t ⟩ , \mathcal{D}_{t}=\langle s_{t},o_{t},r_{t}\rangle, (3) Here, the three components denote dimensions to be operationalised from interaction logs rather than fixed scalar measures: s t s_{t} captures the scope of the control transfer, o t o_{t} the oversight performed after delegating, and r t r_{t} recovery of control and its consequences.
Scope concerns how much of the task is assigned to the AI system and how central that component is to the final outcome. Oversight concerns the checking work performed by the user, including inspection of evidence, revision of AI content, and independent attempts to verify the output. Recovery concerns whether the user detects a problem, interrupts or reverses the AI contribution, and restores human control when needed.

blocks.en: Crucially, these dimensions should be analysed jointly. Indeed, broad delegation followed by timely recovery may reflect more effective oversight than narrow delegation accompanied by no substantive inspection. Moreover, these elements should be interpreted together with the conditions under which delegation takes place. Indeed, in collaborative AI use, the same transfer of control may have different meanings depending on time pressure, perceived AI competence, and the perceived stakes of the task. For the proposed study, we focus on three non-exhaustive contextual factors and associate each episode with a contextual vector: 𝐱 t = ⟨ τ t , γ t , π t ⟩ , \mathbf{x}_{t}=\langle\tau_{t},\gamma_{t},\pi_{t}\rangle, (4) where τ t \tau_{t} denotes time pressure, γ t \gamma_{t} denotes perceived AI competence, and π t \pi_{t} denotes perceived risk or incentive. These factors are important because users may delegate to save time, to compensate for limited expertise, or because the consequences of an error are perceived as tolerable. Conversely, they may retain oversight even under high trust when the task feels consequential or when accountability remains personally salient.
blocks.zh: 至关重要的是,应共同分析这些方面。 实际上,广泛授权以及随后及时追回可能比狭隘授权和不进行实质性检查更加有效的监督。 此外,这些内容应结合进行授权的条件加以解释。 实际上,在人工智能的协作使用中,根据时间压力、人工智能的可感知能力以及任务所感知的利害关系,同样的控制权转移可能具有不同的含义。 对于拟议的研究,我们侧重于三个非详尽的背景因素,并将每集与一个背景矢量联系起来:x t = τ t , γ t , \ t , \ mathbf{ x}_{ t}=\langle\ tau_{t},\gamma_{t},\pi_{t}\rangle, (4) t\tau_{t}表示时间压力, t\gamma_{t}表示感知的AI权限,和 t\pi_{t}表示感知的风险或激励. 这些因素很重要,因为用户可能授权节省时间,补偿有限的专门知识,或者因为误差的后果被认为是可以容忍的。 相反,在任务产生后果或问责制仍然突出的情况下,他们甚至可以保持高度信任的监督。

blocks.en: This formalisation treats delegation as a computational object of human-AI interaction . The task interface we envision to implement this formalisation can reconstruct 𝒟 t \mathcal{D}_{t} from ordinary workflow events. Thus, interaction events such as assigning a component to the AI model, inspecting its output, editing the AI contribution, rejecting generated content, or returning to manual control for completing a task will all have to be recorded by the proposed platform. Specifically, these events should be logged at the adequate level of granularity to reconstruct the moment-by-moment evolution of 𝒟 t \mathcal{D}_{t} . This in-situ reconstruction is important because delegation is rarely a single decision made once at the beginning or end of a task. A participant may initially assign the temporal reconstruction to the AI, then inspect only one critical video segment, accept part of the generated summary, and later reclaim control after noticing a mistake in the model answer. Collapsing this sequence into a final label such as “verified” or “delegated” would miss the trajectory through which oversight was actually performed. Momentary tracking therefore allows delegation to be studied as a dynamic process.
blocks.zh: 这种形式化将授权视为人类-AI相互作用的计算对象。 我们设想执行这种形式化的任务界面可以从普通的工作流程活动中重建 D t \ mathcal{ D}_{t} 。 因此,诸如为AI模型分配一个组件,检查其输出,编辑AI贡献,拒绝生成的内容,或恢复手动控制以完成某项任务等交互事件,都必须被拟议平台记录. 具体地说,这些事件应该记录在足够的颗粒度上,以重建Dt\mathcal{D}_{t}的瞬间进化. 这种就地重建很重要,因为授权很少是在任务开始时或结束时作出的单一决定。 参与者最初可以将时间重建指定给AI,然后只检查一个关键视频段,接受部分生成的概要,然后在发现模型答案错误后恢复控制. 将这一顺序拼凑成“核实”或“授权”等最后标签,将错失实际进行监督的轨道。 因此,跟踪时机可以将授权作为一个动态过程加以研究。

We distinguish this delegation trajectory from the contextual conditions under which it unfolds. This distinction can be expressed schematically as 𝒟 t ∼ p θ ​ ( 𝒟 t ∣ 𝐱 t , 𝐳 t ) , \mathcal{D}_{t}\sim p_{\theta}\!\left(\mathcal{D}_{t}\mid\mathbf{x}_{t},\mathbf{z}_{t}\right), (5) where θ \theta denotes model parameters and 𝐳 t \mathbf{z}_{t} collects additional

This notation keeps delegation analytically distinct from the factors that shape it. Time pressure, for instance, does not constitute delegation by itself, but it may increase the probability of delegation or reduce the degree of inspection post-interaction. Similarly, perceived AI competence may make users more willing to assign central components to the AI, while higher perceived stakes may increase verification, especially after a suspected error. The proposed expression is a
conceptual template for future operationalisation rather than a model estimated in the present study.

blocks.en: In this framing, self-reported trust remains central as a subjective measure, but it should be positioned as complementary to the delegation trace. Sparse trust probes can be collected before the task, at predetermined checkpoints during the interaction, or after controlled failures. This additional recording of trust ratings would reveal regions where self-reported trust and enacted delegation overlap or, more interestingly, diverge. However, we argue that these self-reported ratings should remain sparser and intentional to avoid disrupting the unobtrusive observation of how delegation is embedded in real use, as proposed in the following section.
blocks.zh: 在这一框架中,自我报告的信任作为一项主观措施仍然至关重要,但应将其定位为对代表团追踪的补充。 在任务之前,在互动过程中预先确定的检查站,或在有控制的失败之后,可以收集Sparse信任探测器。 这种对信任评级的额外记录将揭示自报信任和颁布授权重叠或更有趣的是分歧的区域。 然而,我们争辩说,这些自报的评级应该仍然比较少,并且是故意的,以避免干扰对代表团如何真正使用这一无动于衷的观察。

blocks.en: 6 Proposed Study Design for Enacted Delegation
blocks.zh: 6 拟为已颁布的代表团进行的研究设计

blocks.en: Design considerations. The next methodological step is to observe how delegation is enacted while a human and an AI system jointly produce an outcome. As defined in Section 5 , we introduce enacted delegation traces to make observable the transfer of control between human and AI during an ongoing activity. The study we envision should therefore seamlessly integrate delegation as part of the task, rather than an additional question asked after the task has already ended.
blocks.zh: 设计方面的考虑。 下一个方法步骤是观察在人与人工智能系统共同产生结果的同时如何实行权力下放。 正如第5节所定义的,我们引入了已颁布的授权痕迹,以观察在一项持续活动期间人类和大赦国际之间的控制权转移。 因此,我们设想的研究应当将授权完美地纳入任务,而不是在任务结束后再提出另一个问题。

blocks.en: A promising direction is to extend the Video Question Answering setup into a more realistic and gamified learning scenario. Participants could watch short recorded lessons or tutorials and answer a sequence of questions under varying time constraints. Sample questions may require, for instance, locating a specific moment in the video, reconstructing the order of explained steps, or applying concepts explained in the video to a new case. The number of questions could be feasible in the baseline condition and deliberately difficult in groups where we aim to test the effect of time pressure. The interface must also allow for hybrid delegation scenarios: participants could ask the AI to locate relevant video segments, draft an answer, or produce a short explanation, while still being responsible for the final submitted response.
blocks.zh: 一个有希望的方向是将视频问答设置扩展为更加现实和博弈的学习情景. 学员可以观看短篇记录的课程或辅导,并在不同的时间限制下回答一系列问题。 例如,抽样问题可能需要在视频中找到一个特定的时刻,重新编排所解释步骤的顺序,或将视频中解释的概念应用于新案件。 问题的数量在基线条件下可能是可行的,在我们打算测试时间压力影响的小组中是故意困难的。 界面还必须允许混合授权方案:参与者可以要求AI查找相关视频段,起草一个答案,或者制作一个简短的解释,同时仍然负责最后提交的答复.

blocks.en:
This task directly extends the empirical study reported in this paper and can
initially be applied to the same population of AI-literate university students.
This population provides a useful starting point for refining the measures and
interaction traces with users already familiar with AI-supported work. At the same time, it is closer to everyday AI use in educational settings, where students increasingly rely on AI systems to summarise lectures and prepare for assessments. However, the framework is general and can be applied to the study of broader populations, e.g., by integrating more informational and general-purpose videos, or workplace training material.

blocks.en:
The interface should instantiate delegation through ordinary workflow actions mimicking real-world use. Participants should be able to work manually, assign a component to the AI, or take control back after inspecting the AI contribution. Once AI content is available, the participant can inspect the relevant video evidence, revise the answer, or accept the contribution into the final response. The system records
the events needed to reconstruct control transfer and oversight as these unfold. Sparse trust probes can still be collected at specific checkpoints, so that subjective trust remains available without interrupting every micro-decision.

blocks.en: In any case, the interface design should be preceded by a participatory phase. Practical workshops and focus groups can help us identify the situations in which different users already delegate to AI, the moments in which they would like improved and increased oversight of the system. Moreover, there may be key factors shaping delegation in real use beyond time pressure, perceived capability and risk that we may have not anticipated before a focused discussion with users. Users may also respond to boredom, uncertainty about assessment criteria, social norms around acceptable AI use, or effort-related factors, to name just a few. Thus, this participatory phase is instrumental in informing the final task scenarios and control items implemented in the envisaged interface.
blocks.zh: 无论如何,界面设计之前应当有一个参与性阶段。 实际的讲习班和重点小组可以帮助我们确定不同用户已经授权大赦国际处理的情况,以及他们希望改进和加强监督该系统的时刻。 此外,在与用户进行有重点的讨论之前,可能会有关键因素影响权力下放的实际使用,超越时间压力、人们所意识到的能力和风险。 用户也可能对无聊、评估标准不确定、围绕可接受的AI使用的社会规范、或与努力有关的因素作出反应,仅举几个例子。 因此,这一参与阶段有助于为在设想的接口中实施的最后任务设想和控制项目提供信息。

blocks.en: Modelled conditions. An important requirement for conducting the envisaged study is ensuring that specific experimental controls are in place for factors shaping enacted delegation. One way to approach this requirement is to adopt an approach similar to the experimental setup presented in this paper, where participant groups are assigned to different control conditions while seemingly completing the same task. The first condition to test concerns the AI output presentation mode. Depending on the task, the interface could expose AI outputs structured differently: e.g., from a plain textual answer up until a richer interactive workspace where users can view, edit or reject intermediate outputs. This configuration would extend the graph-presentation manipulation used in the preliminary study, while shifting the role of the representation from an explanation shown after the answer to an object through which the user can supervise the collaboration.
blocks.zh: 模拟条件. 进行所设想的研究的一个重要要求是,确保对形成法定授权的因素实行具体的试验性控制。 处理这一要求的一种方法是采取与本文件中介绍的试验设置相似的办法,即各参与小组被分配到不同的控制条件下,同时似乎完成同样的任务。 测试的第一个条件涉及AI输出显示模式. 视任务而定,界面可能暴露出不同结构的AI输出:例如,从一个简单的文字答案上到一个更丰富的交互工作空间,用户可以查看,编辑或拒绝中间输出. 这种配置将扩展初步研究中使用的图解操作,同时将表示的作用从回答后显示的解释转移到用户可以监督协作的对象.

blocks.en: A second ablation concerns the behaviour of the AI assistant. One dimension for controlling the AI behaviour is the injection of incorrect and fabricated answers, similar to the error-injected cohort in our preliminary study. Another dimension is to expose users to different levels of proactive suggestion by the AI, to simulate agentic scenarios. Lastly, another interesting but still underexplored dimension concerns the comparison between a static AI system and adapting AI systems that co-evolve with users.
blocks.zh: 第二项禁令涉及大赦国际助理的行为。 控制AI行为的一个层面是注入不正确和捏造的答案,类似于我们初步研究中输入错误的组别. 另一个层面是让用户接触到AI不同层次的主动建议,模拟代理假想. 最后,另一个令人感兴趣的但仍未得到充分探讨的方面是静态AI系统与与用户共同演化的AI系统之间的比较。

blocks.en: Around these interface and AI-support conditions, the study should explicitly vary task context. Time pressure can be manipulated, for example, by changing the number of questions that must be completed within the available time, making full manual completion difficult in some conditions. Perceived AI competence can be shaped through a pre-task calibration phase in which participants see the assistant’s prior performance on similar tasks. Task stakes can be assessed by introducing reward/penalty schemes, e.g., where participants earn points for correct answers and lose a small number of points when they do not provide supporting evidence alongside the answers. These incentives to make the user’s choices more consequential and engaging ought to be introduced while making sure to keep the interaction between the user and the AI low-risk and non-harmful from an ethical standpoint.
blocks.zh: 围绕这些接口和AI支持条件,研究应明确不同的任务背景. 例如,可以通过改变必须在现有时间内完成的问题数量来操纵时间压力,使在某些情况下完全人工完成困难。 可以通过任务前校准阶段来形成所认为的人工智能能力,在这一阶段,参与者可以看到助理以前执行类似任务的情况。 可以通过实行奖励/惩罚计划来评估任务利害关系,例如,参与者获得正确答案的分数,如果在回答时不提供佐证,则损失少量分数。 这些鼓励措施应使用户的选择更有效果,并让用户参与进来,同时确保用户与AI之间的互动从道德角度讲是低风险和无害的。

blocks.en: The proposed design is different from work on cooperative question answering where delegation is observed mainly as the decision to let the AI answer on behalf of the team Gor et al. (2026) . Here, delegation unfolds within a multimodal workflow in which users transfer control over specific parts of the task, inspect or revise AI contributions, and reclaim control. It also extends work on task delegability and instance-level delegation Lubars and Tan (2019) ; Spitzer et al. (2025) by treating contextual factors as part of the experimental situation rather than as only post-hoc explanations for a final choice. The resulting delegation traces would make it possible to study how human oversight evolves while the task is still in progress.
blocks.zh: 拟议的设计不同于合作问题回答方面的工作,在答复中,代表团主要被视为决定让大赦国际代表Gor等人小组(2026年)作出答复。 在此,权力下放是在一种多式联运工作流程中展开的,在这种工作流程中,用户转移对任务特定部分的控制,检查或修订AI的贡献,并收回控制。 它还通过将背景因素作为实验情况的一部分,而不是作为最后选择的唯一事后解释,扩展了任务可扩展性和实例级代表团Lubars和Tan(2019年);Spitzer等人(2025年)的工作。 由此产生的代表团跟踪将使人们有可能在任务仍在进行时研究人类监督如何演变。

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
This paper started from an empirical study that deliberately focused on
AI-literate users as an initial population for examining how post-interaction
trust relates to intended delegation in repeated Video Question Answering tasks. In this context, the choice to verify the AI outputs remained common even when self-declared trust was high. This pattern suggests that trust is behaviourally consequential, but demands a more systematic study of how human oversight dynamics are embedded in everyday use. The graph comparison adds an XAI-specific observation. Inspectable and editable representations were actively used and were
exploratorily associated with stronger intended delegation, while showing no
reliable association with trust-delegation mismatch. Future evaluations should
therefore examine whether graph inspection helps users identify incorrect
relations, revise the represented evidence, and retain control when errors are
detected.

blocks.en: We thus proposed a shift toward enacted delegation, providing a methodological bridge between subjective trust and human oversight. In this definition, we framed delegation as a traceable redistribution of responsibility across a task, allowing researchers to observe how much work is handed over, to what extent AI outputs are inspected, and whether control can be recovered after failure. This perspective is especially relevant for multimodal and agentic AI systems, where assistance increasingly involves interpreting heterogeneous evidence and acting across several steps of a workflow.
blocks.zh: 因此,我们建议向正式授权转变,在主观信任和人类监督之间提供方法上的桥梁。 在这个定义中,我们把授权定义为可追溯的责任在一项任务中重新分配,使研究人员能够观察移交了多少工作,AI产出被检查的程度,以及失败后能否恢复控制. 这一视角对多式联运和代理性人工智能系统特别相关,在这种系统中,援助越来越多地涉及解释各种证据和跨工作流程的若干步骤采取行动。

blocks.en:
Empirically, we showed that intended delegation captures aspects of repeated human-AI interaction that cannot be reduced to trust ratings. Methodologically, we proposed a framework to be operationalised and validated in future studies of delegation as it is enacted in collaborative multimodal tasks, while controlling for time pressure, perceived AI competence, and task stakes. Although the empirical study began with AI-literate participants, the proposed
framework is intended to support comparative studies across populations with
different levels of AI familiarity and domain expertise.

blocks.en: Our broader aim is to encourage discussion on evaluating multimodal, explainable, and agentic AI systems in terms of the quality of oversight they support. Enacted delegation offers one way to make this quality observable by turning the small, distributed decisions through which users retain or transfer control in everyday AI use into a measurable object of human-centred interaction research.
blocks.zh: 我们更广泛的目标是鼓励就评价多式联运、可解释性和代理性人工智能系统所支持的监督质量进行讨论。 通过将用户在日常AI使用中保留或转移控制权的小型、分布式决定转变为以人为中心的互动研究的可衡量目标,由官方代表团提供一种方法,使这种质量得到观察。
